request: Make the source-scanning tests line-ending agnostic so they pass on a CRLF checkout
checks: npm run check passed end to end: typecheck, build, 415/415 tests, validate (31 build files, 4 React entry points, service-worker imports)

npm test went from 411/415 to 415/415; no test was weakened - verified independently that the code satisfies all three assertions (0 chrome.downloads in applicants.js, 0 DOM refs in applicants-core.js, 2 visibility guards in background.ts)
git diff --check passed; only the two test files changed, no production source touched, no secrets
result: Fixed the 4 failing tests. Root cause was line endings, not logic: the repo is LF-canonical but core.autocrlf=true checks the tree out as CRLF, and '.' does not match CR, so withoutComments() left every '// ...' comment intact and three 'this file must never mention X' assertions read the sentence explaining the absence as the thing itself; a fourth regex used a bare backslash-n and matched neither visibility guard. Normalized line endings in withoutComments() and made the collector-tabs guard regex accept CR-LF. No production code was touched - applicants.js has 0 chrome.downloads, applicants-core.js has 0 DOM references and background.ts has both visibility guards, all verified independently.
